Landscape on a river network

Source: R/river.R
landscape_river.Rd

Builds a landscape whose sites lie on a dendritic river network, with dispersal along the channel that can differ upstream and downstream, as in the riverine metacommunities of Carrara et al. (2012) and Altermatt (2013). The probability that an emigrant from site s reaches site t is proportional to $$\exp\left(-\frac{d_{\downarrow}}{s_{\downarrow}} - \frac{d_{\uparrow}}{s_{\uparrow}} \right),$$ where \(d_\downarrow\) is the distance it travels downstream (from s to the confluence where the paths of s and t meet) and \(d_\uparrow\) the distance it then travels upstream (from the confluence to t). A scale_up smaller than scale_down gives the drift of passive dispersers, and equal scales a symmetric kernel along the channel. A share overland of emigrants instead moves in a straight line, with an exponential kernel of the straight-line distance (scale overland_scale), for organisms with an aerial or terrestrial stage that can cross between branches.

Usage

landscape_river(
  network = river_network(50),
  env = NULL,
  scale_down = 2,
  scale_up = scale_down,
  overland = 0,
  overland_scale = 1,
  env_range = c(0, 100)
)

Arguments

network

A data frame with one row per site and the columns downstream (row of the downstream neighbour, NA for the single outlet) and length (of the reach to the downstream neighbour), and optionally x and y; for instance from river_network(). Without x and y, coordinates are laid out as in river_network().

env

Numeric vector with the environment of each site, or NULL (the default) for the distance from the outlet along the channel rescaled to env_range, a gradient from the lowlands to the headwaters.

scale_down, scale_up

Scales of the kernel for the distance travelled downstream and upstream, in the units of length.

overland

Share of emigrants that move in a straight line rather than along the channel (between 0 and 1).

overland_scale

Scale of the exponential kernel of straight-line dispersal.

env_range

Range of the environment when env is NULL.

Value

An mc_landscape object, as from landscape_matrix(), whose dist holds the distances along the channel and which also keeps network (the network completed as in river_network()) and downstream (sites x sites matrix of the distance travelled downstream from the site in the row to the site in the column; its transpose is the distance travelled upstream).

References

Altermatt, F. (2013). Diversity in riverine metacommunities: a network perspective. Aquatic Ecology, 47, 365–377. doi:10.1007/s10452-013-9450-3

Carrara, F., Altermatt, F., Rodriguez-Iturbe, I., & Rinaldo, A. (2012). Dendritic connectivity controls biodiversity patterns in experimental metacommunities. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 109, 5761–5766. doi:10.1073/pnas.1119651109

See also

Other landscapes: dispersal_kernel(), env_over_time(), env_pulse(), env_river(), env_seasonal(), env_space_time(), landscape_grid(), landscape_implicit(), landscape_matrix(), landscape_points(), river_covariance(), river_floods(), river_network()

Examples

set.seed(1)
land <- landscape_river(river_network(40), scale_down = 3, scale_up = 1)
land
#> <mc_landscape> 40 sites; river network (9 headwaters) 
#> environment:    0 to 100 
# emigrants from a headwater go mostly downstream
head(order(-land$dispersal[which.max(land$network$distance), ]))
#> [1] 18 11  9 16  6 19
traits <- data.frame(optimum = c(20, 50, 80), sigma = 20, r_max = 4,
                     row.names = paste0("sp", 1:3))
alpha <- matrix(0.05, 3, 3, dimnames = list(rownames(traits), rownames(traits)))
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.1, n_steps = 100)
